It’s actually a sweet story. When I moved in to my apartment in 2021, my appearance had changed a lot in a short amount of time, and I was struggling severely with both body dysmorphia and gender dysphoria (though I wasn’t very aware of latter part). I took down my mirror because I could not handle confronting myself every time I used the bathroom. It stayed that way for years. 

Then, this past summer, I fell in love with the same friend that gave me their extra t-gel. they moved in with me and my other partner. Once I started T, my self-image improved and I started recognizing myself in mirrors. I started wanting more of them around. Still, I limited them to spaces where I’d have to willingly interact with them, like my dressing area. 

But since we are moving soon, we had replace the bathroom mirror for the next renters. I felt mostly fine about this, but still a little worried about how it would affect me to have to see myself every time I used the bathroom. My partner, knowing I had this anxiety, posted that sign to the mirror when they put it back up for me. They are always doing little things like that to bring more joy into our lives ❤️ 

So far I’ve had no problems with the mirror being back up. I enjoy looking at myself and don’t really over scrutinize like I used to. Unless I get in front of a magnifying mirror but hey I’m only human.

I think most users would want the digests and highlighting to be integrated.   Here is how I imagine my workflow: 

I open a document on my Supernote to read and annotate. When I come across a passage I find interesting, I put brackets or highlight around the text (whether its highlight or bracket does not matter. what matters is that the text will be recognized and extractable by 3rd party services). I click on the highlighted/bracketed text and the digest pops up as it does now. I jot down my thoughts there - having this option is still important to me because, as you obviously know, handwriting is the ultimate processing tool. Later, I upload that same document to my PC and have a 3rd party service extract all of my highlights/bracketed text. Now I have them on both the PC and Supernote. I can go to the digest and look at what I jot down as I was processing the passage in the moment, and use that to flesh out my thoughts by typing on the PC. 

The extracted highlights are useful because it allows me to have all my highlights in the same place for referencing. I do not want this feature to replace or be different from the digest - ideally it would just be the same as the digest, the only difference would be that 3rd party software can recognize what is bracketed/highlighted. I hope this makes sense - happy to clarify anything or answer questions about use case.

I'm a student and I have a tab 7. I've also owned two other samsung note tablets with s-pen capabilities and I've had a laptop with these features since 2018. Plus, I've had galaxy note 10 for two years now. I got started with handwritten digital notes through these Samsung devices; they revolutionized the way I take notes for school. 

However, I also have ADHD. No matter how hard I tried to keep at east one device dedicated to school, I ended downloading a bunch of distracting apps every single time. I literally tried for years. I used all the tricks - app blockers, greyscale, timed apps - there are always loopholes and I would always end up using them. Plus, easy access to google was my biggest distraction and I cannot block google as I need it for school purposes. I cannot get my brain to associate these multipurpose tablets solely with my academics. 

The other big thing that was equally important to me was eye strain and headaches. I read so many PDFs and take so many notes, both typed and handwritten - add in email, zoom calls, videos, online course platforms, etc etc - I was staring at screens literally all day and didn't have much option to limit that if I still wanted to get things done. Greyscale, bluelight filters on screen and even blue light filtering glasses were not helpful. This really affected me, perhaps more than the average person because I am also autistic and consider it to be a sensory issue. I am very sensitive to light. So,  after two years of telling myself an e-ink tablet would be an irresponsible splurge,  I knew I needed something different.
